text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000016 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, but with only one documented 99215 chart the records are too thin to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 rate holds in every complexity tier with one or more chronic conditions and is steepest among 3+ condition patients, so complexity alone does not explain it. Most 99215s fall on multi-morbid patients, and the low-complexity share noted above is small, which fits a demanding panel at least as well as systematic inflation. The overall mix is also heavily weighted to 99214, which deserves attention alongside the 99215 share. The documentation cannot settle the question: one 99215 chart (C0005777) supports its level and one 99214 chart (C0006167) was documented below the billed level, but these are single claims. The data-reviewed notes all matched lab or test lines on the claim, so there is no cloning signal. A reviewer should first request a larger chart sample weighted toward 99215 and 99214 claims, starting with the 0–1 condition 99215s billed for minor diagnoses (for example C0005324 J06.9, C0006268 R10.9, C0007603 M54.50, C0007454 Z09), to see whether the documented MDM supports the billed level."}
